name: si.opencheap/opencheap
title: OpenCheap
description: One API key for every AI model, routed to the cheapest provider. OpenAI-compatible.

tools.name: get_account
tools.description:
Get the account

The account, its prepaid balance (your calls and your customers' calls are debited from it), what it spent this calendar month at our price, and its default gateway.

tools.name: update_account
tools.description:
Update the account

Changes the account name, the low-balance alert threshold and the default gateway. Fields left out are unchanged; `name: null` clears the name, `defaultGateway: null` the default gateway. The order a request runs under: its x-klinn-gateway header, else its key's gateway, else the account's default gateway. A default gateway with guardrails locks the keys under it: a header naming another gateway is 403 gateway_locked.

defaultGateway.description: A chat gateway's name to make the account's default (every own model key without a gateway of its own runs through it), or null to clear it. A decisions gateway is refused: attach it to a key instead.

tools.name: get_balance
tools.description:
Get the balance

The prepaid balance and how to top it up from code: over x402 with USDC (when switched on) or with a card link for a person (the `create_topup_checkout` tool). Takes an agent session or a management key like every v1 operation; a model key gets 403 wrong_key_type. Also served at /v1/balance, which also accepts the account's model keys (kl_live_).

tools.name: list_budgets
tools.description:
List budgets

The account's budget (null without one) and each of the account's working model keys, its customers' keys included, with its budget (null without one), each limit with what was spent in its current window, at our price. Every key is listed, not paged; each one takes the `set_key_budget` tool. A key's monthly limit is the key's monthlyLimitUsd (the same cap create_key sets). Windows are UTC: the day from midnight, the week from Monday, the month from the 1st, lifetime from when that limit was set.

tools.name: get_account_budget
tools.description:
Get the account budget

The account's budget: every key's spend together, its customers' keys included (their calls debit the account's balance), with each limit's spend this window. 404 not_found when the account has none. Windows are UTC: the day from midnight, the week from Monday, the month from the 1st, lifetime from when that limit was set.

tools.name: set_account_budget
tools.description:
Set the account budget

Sets or replaces the account's budget: daily, weekly, monthly and lifetime limits at our price (at least one), the alert share and the mode. hard_stop refuses the key's requests with a 402 once a limit is reached (the request that crosses it can go a little over: the check runs before a request, its cost lands after, and the Model API keeps the key's state for about a minute); alert_only never blocks and sends one email per limit and window when the spend crosses alertPct. A limit left out or null is no limit. Requests follow within about a minute.

limits.description: Limits in USD at our price, to the cent. At least one; null or left out is no limit.

weekly.description: Per ISO week, from Monday 00:00 UTC.

monthly.description: Per calendar month, from the 1st 00:00 UTC. On a key, this is its monthlyLimitUsd.

lifetime.description: For good, from when this limit was set.

alertPct.description: Email once per limit and window when the spend crosses this share of a limit. 0 turns the alert off.

mode.description: hard_stop refuses requests with a 402 at a limit; alert_only never blocks (it needs alertPct above 0).

idempotencyKey.description: Optional. A unique string so that repeating this call never creates twice.

tools.name: remove_account_budget
tools.description:
Remove the account budget

Removes the account's budget: the keys' own budgets stay. 404 not_found when there is none. 204 with no body.

tools.name: list_customers
tools.description:
List customers

Your customers, newest first. Filter by your own id (externalRef, exact), a search over name, email and externalRef (q, case-insensitive), or status.

cursor.description: The `nextCursor` of the previous page, unchanged.

externalRef.description: Exact match on your own id.

q.description: Case-insensitive substring of name, email or externalRef.

tools.name: create_customer
tools.description:
Create a customer

Creates a customer (201): a group of keys with its own monthly limit, balance record and usage. With an externalRef that already exists, returns that one with 200 instead, so a signup webhook can be retried safely. Its usage is debited directly from your balance at our price, so its keys work without any credit. With billingMode limit, or a spendLimitUsd sent alone, spendLimitUsd caps its monthly usage (PATCH sets it for any customer). initialCreditUsd only records a payment for your books. Amounts are at our price. At most 10,000 customers per account: past it, 409 limit_reached.

externalRef.description: Your own id. Creating a customer with an externalRef that already exists returns that one (200) instead of a new one, so a signup webhook can be retried safely.

initialCreditUsd.description: billingMode prepaid only: a payment to record as the opening balanceUsd. Not needed for its keys to work. 0, or from 0.00000001 to less than 1,000,000.

spendLimitUsd.description: billingMode limit only: monthly spending cap at our price. PATCH sets it for any customer.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional. A unique string so that repeating this call never creates twice.

tools.name: get_customer
tools.description:
Get a customer

One of your customers.

tools.name: update_customer
tools.description:
Update a customer

Changes only the fields you send. Pause a customer to stop its keys; spendLimitUsd sets its monthly limit and null removes it.

externalRef.description: Must be unique per account (409 conflict otherwise); null clears it.

spendLimitUsd.description: Monthly spending cap at our price; null removes it.

tools.name: delete_customer
tools.description:
Delete a customer

Deletes the customer, its balance history and all its keys, which stop working at once. Cannot be undone.

tools.name: credit_customer
tools.description:
Record a customer payment

Records on balanceUsd a payment (positive) or a correction (negative). For your books only: its calls never draw on it and are not blocked at zero, because its usage is debited directly from your balance. Your own balance is untouched. Idempotency-Key is required so a retry never records twice. Returns the customer.

amountUsd.description: Non-zero (at least 0.00000001 either way) and less than 1,000,000 either way. Positive to record a payment; negative to correct. 400 when balanceUsd would leave the range -999,999.99999999 to 999,999.99999999.

note.description: Shown in the customer's ledger. Defaults to Credit or Debit.

idempotencyKey.description: Required. A unique string for this change (e.g. the payment id): repeating it never applies the change twice.

tools.name: list_customer_keys
tools.description:
List a customer's keys

The customer's model keys, newest first: working keys only unless includeRevoked=true. Secrets are never shown again.

tools.name: create_customer_key
tools.description:
Create a key for a customer

Creates a model key for the customer. The secret is in this response only. Calls with it are billed to your balance at our price. At most 50 working keys per customer, and 5,000 new customer keys a day per account: past either, 409 limit_reached.

allowedModels.description: Models the key may call; null or empty for every model.

monthlyLimitUsd.description: Monthly cap of this key at our price (what its calls cost you), calendar month; null for none. spendLimitUsd caps the whole customer.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional. A unique string so that repeating this call never creates twice.

tools.name: revoke_customer_key
tools.description:
Revoke a customer's key

Revokes the key; it stops working at once. 404 when the key is not this customer's or is already revoked.

tools.name: list_customer_ledger
tools.description:
List a customer's recorded payments

Payments and corrections you recorded for this customer, newest first. Its usage is not here: it is debited from your balance (see /ledger and /usage).

cursor.description: The `nextCursor` of the previous page, unchanged.

tools.name: list_gateways
tools.description:
List gateways

Every gateway of the account, A to Z by name, with its kind, its default model and how many rules, questions and keys it has. A gateway is a named config a request runs through. A chat gateway (kind chat) routes the chat and messages calls your code sends: fallbacks between models, retries, a response cache, a rate limit, a time limit and the models allowed. A decision gateway (kind decision) is your own classifier: it keeps a decision model and the questions, so a call to the decisions endpoint sends only the text. Attach one to a key as its default (the `update_key` tool) or name it per request with the x-klinn-gateway header; the header wins, except on a key locked to its gateway. A key with a gateway of its own, or under an account default gateway with guardrails, is locked to it: a header naming another is a 403 gateway_locked.

tools.name: create_gateway
tools.description:
Create a gateway

Saves a new gateway from its config, validated and normalized; the stored config comes back. The name is its id here and in the x-klinn-gateway header: a-z, 0-9 and -, at most 48 characters, and not new, playground, rules or templates (the console's own pages); a name already in use is 409 conflict. A chat gateway needs only a name; a fallback or a split needs at least two targets. A decision gateway (kind decision) needs a default_model that is a decision model (kind decisions in the `list_models` tool) and 1 to 128 questions. At most 50 gateways an account. Keys are attached with the `update_key` tool. At most 50 gateways per account: past it, 409 limit_reached.

name.description: Its id in this API and in the x-klinn-gateway header: 1 to 48 characters of a-z, 0-9 and -, starting and ending with a letter or digit. new, playground, rules and templates are reserved for the console's own pages: a new gateway or a rename cannot take them.

kind.description: chat routes the requests your code sends; decision is a classifier: its default model is a decision model and its questions are saved here.

default_model.description: The model a request with model "default" (or none) gets; null for the request's own model. A decision gateway needs one, and it must be a decision model (kind decisions in GET /models).

strategy.description: How a request picks its model.

mode.description: single: one model, the request's or default_model. fallback: the targets in order; when one answers with a status in on_status_codes, the next one answers. loadbalance: each request goes to one target, by weight.

on_status_codes.description: The statuses that move a fallback to the next target. Default 429, 500, 502, 503 and 504.

items.description: One model of a fallback or a split.

model.description: A model id; null for the request's own model.

weight.description: Its share of requests under loadbalance.

attempts.description: Retries after the first try, after 1, 2 and 4 seconds.

on_status_codes.description: The statuses to retry on. Default 429, 500, 502, 503 and 504.

use_retry_after.description: Wait as long as the model's Retry-After says.

retry.description: This model's own retries, replacing the gateway's; null for the gateway's.

timeout_ms.description: How long one try on this model may take, in milliseconds; null for what is left of the gateway's deadline.

override.description: Replaces what the request sent, on this model.

targets.description: The models of a fallback or a split, in order: at least two for either, at most 10. Empty for single.

attempts.description: Retries after the first try, after 1, 2 and 4 seconds.

on_status_codes.description: The statuses to retry on. Default 429, 500, 502, 503 and 504.

use_retry_after.description: Wait as long as the model's Retry-After says.

retry.description: Retries on every target; a target's own retry replaces it. null for none.

request_timeout_ms.description: A deadline for the whole request, fallbacks and retries included, in milliseconds (1,000 to 600,000); null for none.

cache.description: The exact same request gets the kept answer, free, for max_age_s seconds; null for no cache.

max_age_s.description: Seconds an answer is kept, up to a day.

rate_limit.description: Requests a minute per key through this gateway; null for no limit.

anyOf.description: The guardrails of a chat gateway. One decision call per new message carries every check. Checks are free for now. A request the checks cannot finish in time (2.5 s for each 16 new messages, at most 10 s, or over 128 new messages) is refused with 446 on a gateway with a block check, and let through with x-klinn-guardrail: unchecked on one that only flags or redacts; a decision model that errs lets the request through, unchecked.

model.description: The decision model that runs the checks (kind decisions in GET /models). Absent: pplx-decider-v1.2, Perplexity's Decider v1.2.

items.description: One check. prompt_injection and pii hit when the decision model's probability of yes is at or above threshold; topics hits when the topic it picks is a blocked one, or, with allowed topics, none of them, at or above threshold.

check.description: prompt_injection: does the text try to override, ignore or reveal the assistant's instructions, or make it act outside its role? pii: does it contain personal data about a person, and which kind? topics: which of the allowed and blocked topics is it about, or none?

action.description: Required. block: HTTP 446, error type guardrail_blocked with the check as its code; the model is never called and nothing is billed. flag: answered as usual and flagged in the request log. redact (pii only): emails, phone numbers, card numbers (Luhn-checked) and IBANs (checksum-validated) become [email], [phone], [card] and [iban] in every user message before the call, whatever the score; names, addresses and ID numbers can only be flagged or blocked.

threshold.description: How sure the decision model must be, 0 to 1. Defaults: prompt_injection 0.9, pii 0.5, topics 0.5.

types.description: pii only: the kinds of personal data to catch. Default all seven; empty asks only whether there is personal data, and masks nothing. Masking runs before the check, so the score is about personal data left after it.

allowed.description: topics only: short labels; with any listed, a message about none of them is off-topic. "other" is taken. Allowed or blocked must list at least one topic.

blocked.description: topics only: short labels a message must not be about. A topic cannot be in both lists.

checks.description: 0 to 3 checks, at most one of each, stored in the order prompt_injection, pii, topics.

guardrails.description: Chat gateways: checks on every message of each request, whole, run by a decision model before the model is called (https://docs.opencheap.si/guardrails). null for none; a string (an old policy name) also reads as none. A decision gateway takes none: its /v1/systemone calls are not checked.

allow_models.description: Model ids, or patterns with *, the gateway lets through; any other model is 403 model_not_allowed. null for any model.

log_bodies.description: Logging prompts and answers is not available yet: leave it false.

community_supply.description: Whether community-supplied capacity (first-party vendor capacity other accounts list, under the same no-training terms) may serve requests under this gateway. Left out: on. A decision gateway never uses it: it may not be set true there.

max_price.description: The default limit order of chat requests under this gateway: they are billed at most this per 1M tokens, or refused with 422 no_offer_under_limit when nothing in the market is within it. It replaces the key's maxPrice; a request's own limit (its max_price field or the x-max-price header) comes first. Left out: none. Not on a decision gateway.

cache.description: USD per 1M input tokens read from the cache. A route that bills cached tokens at its input price is compared at that price.

prompt.description: The compatible name for input; returned under this name.

completion.description: The compatible name for output; returned under this name.

input_cache_read.description: The compatible name for cache; returned under this name.

cache_read.description: Another name for cache, accepted on input.

min_discount.description: The default minimum discount of chat requests under this gateway: they are served only at least this many percent under the model's list price, or refused with 422 no_offer_under_limit when nothing in the market is. The strictest of it, the key's minDiscount and the request's own (the min_discount field or the x-min-discount header) applies. Left out: none. Not on a decision gateway.

speed.description: The default speed of chat requests under this gateway: how they pick among routes ({sort, minThroughput, maxLatencySecs}; cheapest, balanced, fastest or a custom floor and ceiling, see /docs/speed). It comes before the key's speed, field by field: a floor or ceiling it leaves out falls to the key's. A request's own sort, min_throughput and max_latency settings come first, then a :nitro / :floor model suffix. An explicit {sort: price} puts the sort back to cheapest over a faster key. max_price still caps the price. Left out: none. Not on a decision gateway.

sort.description: What the routes are ordered by.

minThroughput.description: Tokens per second a route should reach; null for no floor.

maxLatencySecs.description: Seconds to the first token a route should stay within; null for no ceiling.

io_ratio.description: The expected input:output token ratio of chat requests under this gateway, as input tokens per output token (15 for 15:1). Their routes are ranked at it instead of at max_tokens (see /docs/speed#io-ratio). It replaces the key's ioRatio; a request's own x-klinn-io-ratio header comes first. Ranking only: holds, limits, max_price and the bill are unchanged. Left out: none. Not on a decision gateway.

zdr.description: Zero data retention: requests under this gateway are kept off community-supplied capacity.

data.description: Data handling. Left out: no constraint.

region.description: A region pin: eu keeps requests under this gateway off community-supplied capacity. Left out or null: none.

instructions.description: Decision gateways: a context line, what the text is. Left out when empty.

type.description: choice: one of the options. score: a number from 0 to 1, or a place on the levels listed, lowest first. noul: yes or no, as a probability.

options.description: choice: 2 to 64 options. score: 2 to 10 levels, lowest first, optional. noul: none. Each at most 80 characters, none twice.

questions.description: Decision gateways: the questions by name (1 to 40 characters of a-z, 0-9 and _, starting with a letter), 1 to 128 of them.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional. A unique string so that repeating this call never creates twice.

tools.name: get_gateway
tools.description:
Get a gateway

The gateway's stored config (what create and replace accept, normalized), the ids of the keys it is the default of, and when it was created and last changed.

tools.name: update_gateway
tools.description:
Replace a gateway

Replaces the whole config: send the config from the `get_gateway` tool with your changes. Fields left out take their defaults and the same checks apply as on create. A body without a name keeps this one; a different name renames the gateway (a name already in use is 409 conflict) and its keys follow. Keys stay attached either way. Requests follow the new config within about a minute: the router keeps a key's gateway and the account's gateway list for about 60 seconds, so until then a request may still run through the old config.

tools.name: delete_gateway
tools.description:
Delete a gateway

Deletes it. Keys that had it as their default go back to none, so their requests run as without a gateway; a request still naming it is refused by the Model API (400 gateway_not_found). Both follow within about a minute: the router keeps a key's gateway and the account's gateway list for about 60 seconds, so until then a request may still run through the deleted gateway. 204 with no body.

tools.name: gateway_decisions
tools.description:
Get a decision gateway's answers

How a decision gateway answered over the last 24 hours or 7 days: for each question of its config, how many requests answered it and, for a choice or a yes/no question, each answer's count, most frequent first (at most 12, the rest as other); for a score, the mean and the share at or above 0.5. requests counts the decisions calls through the gateway in the range. A chat gateway answers 400 invalid_request.

range.description: The last 24 hours (per hour) or the last 7 days (per day).

tools.name: gateway_stats
tools.description:
Get gateway stats

What the gateway did over the last 24 hours (per hour) or 7 days (per day), from the request log: requests (a refused one counts its repeats), p95 latency, the error rate, the cache hit rate and how many requests were blocked; then each routing rule's count over the range and per bucket: fell back, retried (and how many retries), answered from cache (savedUsd: what the hits would have cost at the model's average price), rate limited, refused as not allowed, timed out, and the split per model. The same numbers as the console's gateway page.

range.description: The last 24 hours (per hour) or the last 7 days (per day).

tools.name: list_instances
tools.description:
List instances

The account's instances, running ones first, then the newest. A running instance is billed up to now when read, so billedSeconds and billedUsd are current.

status.description: Only running or only stopped ones.

tools.name: start_instance
tools.description:
Start an instance

Starts a machine for one model: gpuClass (default h200) and size (eighths of a node, default 1) pick its spec and price, fixed for as long as it runs. Billing is per second while it runs, one minute at least: the first minute is debited at once. From the next call on (within a few seconds), the account's calls to that model through any of its model keys cost nothing per token and are held to the machine's limits instead (429 with Retry-After past one). It runs until stopped (stop_instance), until its hours pass, or until the balance runs out. One running instance per model: a second start of the same model is a 409 conflict naming the running one. 402 insufficient_balance when the balance does not cover the first minute; 503 not_configured while no price is known for the model.

gpuClass.description: The node class the machine is sized like: one the model is offered on (its machines in list_instance_types). Absent: the model's own class.

size.description: Eighths of a node: 1 is 1/8 node, 2 a quarter, 4 a half, 8 a full node.

hours.description: How long it runs, in hours from now (0.25 is 15 minutes, 2 is two hours); it stops by itself then. Null or absent: it runs until you stop it or the balance runs out. Billing is per second either way.

instanceName.description: Your name for it, shown in the console's history and the API.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional. A unique string so that repeating this call never creates twice.

tools.name: get_instance
tools.description:
Get an instance

One instance, billed up to now when it runs.

tools.name: update_instance
tools.description:
Set an instance's timer

Sets when a running instance stops by itself: hours from now (to extend it, or shorten it), or null to run until stopped. The price and limits stay as they are; billing stays per second. 409 conflict when it has already stopped.

hours.description: Hours from now until it stops by itself; null: it runs until you stop it.

tools.name: stop_instance
tools.description:
Stop an instance

Stops it now and bills it to this second (one minute at least). From the next call on, calls to its model are billed per token again. Stopping a stopped instance answers it as it is.

tools.name: request_dedicated_hardware
tools.description:
Ask for dedicated hardware

Tells OpenCheap the account would rent dedicated hardware: the GPU class, region, model and hours a month. Stored, and answered by email to the account's address. Starts nothing and bills nothing.

model.description: The model to run (any id, or a name).

tools.name: list_instance_types
tools.description:
List instance types

What can be started: each model with its machines. A machine is sized like a share of one 8-GPU node of a class (gpuClass: the class the model is offered on; size in eighths of a node: 1, 2, 4 or 8) and has a spec (parallel streams, target output tokens a second per stream, context), the limits that follow from it, and our price per hour and per second (null while no price is known). Prices follow the market and are fixed for an instance once it starts. available is false while instances are not open yet.

tools.name: list_keys
tools.description:
List model keys

The account's own model keys (`kl_live_…`), newest first. Customer keys are listed under /customers/{id}/keys and management keys under /management-keys. Revoked keys are left out unless `includeRevoked=true`.

cursor.description: The `nextCursor` of the previous page, unchanged.

tools.name: create_key
tools.description:
Create a model key

Creates a model key for the account itself. The `secret` is returned once, in this response; a replay with the same Idempotency-Key returns the key with `secret: null`. Customer keys are created under /customers/{id}/keys. `maxPrice` gives it a default limit order (the most its requests are billed per 1M tokens), `minDiscount` a default minimum discount (its requests are served only at least that many percent under a model's list price), `speed` a default speed (how its requests pick among routes: cheapest, balanced, fastest or a custom floor and ceiling; see /docs/speed), and `ioRatio` its expected input:output ratio (15 or "15:1": routes are ranked at the prompt divided by it instead of at max_tokens; see /docs/speed#io-ratio). At most 500 model keys per account, and 1,000 new ones a day (revoked ones count): past either, 409 limit_reached.

allowedModels.description: Limit the key to these model ids; null or empty for all.

monthlyLimitUsd.description: Spend cap per calendar month; null or 0 for none.

oneOf.description: A limit order's maximum price: the most a request is billed per 1M tokens, on the input leg, the output leg, the cache leg or several (at least one), each compared on its own. Send {"input", "output", "cache"}; the compatible names prompt, completion and input_cache_read (also cache_read) are the same legs and are accepted too, but a leg given under two names with different values is a 400. It is stored and returned under the compatible names (prompt, completion, input_cache_read). A request nothing in the market is within is refused with 422 no_offer_under_limit and billed nothing; a request with no limit is matched at the market price.

cache.description: USD per 1M input tokens read from the cache. A route that bills cached tokens at its input price is compared at that price.

prompt.description: The compatible name for input; returned under this name.

completion.description: The compatible name for output; returned under this name.

input_cache_read.description: The compatible name for cache; returned under this name.

cache_read.description: Another name for cache, accepted on input.

maxPrice.description: The key's default limit order (see Key.maxPrice); null or left out for none.

minDiscount.description: The key's default minimum discount, 0 to 100 (see Key.minDiscount); null or left out for none.

oneOf.description: How requests pick among the routes that can serve a model. `sort` orders the routes: `price` (cheapest first, the default), `throughput` (fastest tokens per second first; the :nitro suffix) or `latency` (quickest to the first token first). `minThroughput` and `maxLatencySecs` are best effort: routes that meet them come first, and when none does the request is still served by the next best route. A request that sets allow_fallbacks to false makes them strict instead (503 no_route_meets_speed). Community-supplied routes must also reach at least half the model's median speed to get traffic. Balanced is {sort: price, minThroughput: 30}; Fastest is {sort: throughput}. max_price still caps the price.

sort.description: What the routes are ordered by.

minThroughput.description: Tokens per second a route should reach; null for no floor.

maxLatencySecs.description: Seconds to the first token a route should stay within; null for no ceiling.

speed.description: The key's default speed (see Key.speed); null or left out for none.

priceFallover.description: The key's price fall-over (see Key.priceFallover); null or left out for the default (on).

ioRatio.description: The key's expected input:output ratio (see Key.ioRatio), as a number of input tokens per output token or a string such as "15:1"; null or left out for none.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional. A unique string so that repeating this call never creates twice.

tools.name: update_key
tools.description:
Set a model key's gateway, supply, price, speed or input:output ratio

Changes one of the account's own model keys: `gateway` sets or clears the gateway it runs through by default (a gateway's name from the `list_gateways` tool, or null for none; requests on the key then go through it, and a request naming another with the x-klinn-gateway header is refused with 403 gateway_locked), `communitySupply` sets whether community-supplied capacity may serve its requests (false keeps every request on our own routes), and `maxPrice` sets or clears its default limit order ({input, output, cache} USD per 1M tokens; prompt, completion and input_cache_read are accepted too: a request nothing in the market is within is refused with 422 no_offer_under_limit and billed nothing). `minDiscount` sets or clears its default minimum discount (0 to 100: its requests are served only at least that many percent under a model's list price; the same 422 when nothing in the market is). `speed` sets or clears its default speed ({sort, minThroughput, maxLatencySecs}: a request's own settings and its gateway's come first; see /docs/speed). `priceFallover` sets whether its requests may go to a dearer source when none can serve them at the model's price (false keeps them at the model's price, null returns to the default, on; see /docs/errors#fallover). `ioRatio` sets or clears its expected input:output ratio (a number such as 15, or a string such as "15:1" or "1:4": routes are ranked at the prompt divided by it instead of at max_tokens; a request's own x-klinn-io-ratio header and its gateway's io_ratio come first; see /docs/speed#io-ratio). Each field changes only when given; give at least one. New requests follow within about a minute. A name no gateway of yours has is 400 invalid_request; a revoked key, a customer's key or an unknown id is 404. Returns the key.

gateway.description: The name of the gateway the key's requests run through by default (one of GET /gateways), or null for none.

communitySupply.description: Whether community-supplied capacity may serve the key's requests; false keeps every request on our own routes. New requests follow within about a minute.

oneOf.description: A limit order's maximum price: the most a request is billed per 1M tokens, on the input leg, the output leg, the cache leg or several (at least one), each compared on its own. Send {"input", "output", "cache"}; the compatible names prompt, completion and input_cache_read (also cache_read) are the same legs and are accepted too, but a leg given under two names with different values is a 400. It is stored and returned under the compatible names (prompt, completion, input_cache_read). A request nothing in the market is within is refused with 422 no_offer_under_limit and billed nothing; a request with no limit is matched at the market price.

cache.description: USD per 1M input tokens read from the cache. A route that bills cached tokens at its input price is compared at that price.

prompt.description: The compatible name for input; returned under this name.

completion.description: The compatible name for output; returned under this name.

input_cache_read.description: The compatible name for cache; returned under this name.

cache_read.description: Another name for cache, accepted on input.

maxPrice.description: The key's default limit order: the most its requests are billed per 1M tokens, per leg; null clears it. A request's own limit and its gateway's come first. New requests follow within about a minute.

minDiscount.description: The key's default minimum discount, 0 to 100: its requests are served only at least this many percent under a model's list price; null clears it. A request's own and its gateway's can only make it stricter. New requests follow within about a minute.

oneOf.description: How requests pick among the routes that can serve a model. `sort` orders the routes: `price` (cheapest first, the default), `throughput` (fastest tokens per second first; the :nitro suffix) or `latency` (quickest to the first token first). `minThroughput` and `maxLatencySecs` are best effort: routes that meet them come first, and when none does the request is still served by the next best route. A request that sets allow_fallbacks to false makes them strict instead (503 no_route_meets_speed). Community-supplied routes must also reach at least half the model's median speed to get traffic. Balanced is {sort: price, minThroughput: 30}; Fastest is {sort: throughput}. max_price still caps the price.

sort.description: What the routes are ordered by.

minThroughput.description: Tokens per second a route should reach; null for no floor.

maxLatencySecs.description: Seconds to the first token a route should stay within; null for no ceiling.

speed.description: The key's default speed ({sort, minThroughput, maxLatencySecs}); null clears it. A request's own settings and its gateway's come first. New requests follow within about a minute.

priceFallover.description: Whether the key's requests may go to a dearer source when none can serve them at the model's price: false keeps them at the model's price, true allows it, null returns to the default (on). The request's own allow_price_fallover setting, and any price limit, come first. New requests follow within about a minute.

ioRatio.description: The key's expected input:output ratio, as a number of input tokens per output token (15) or a string such as "15:1" or "1:4"; null clears it. A request's own x-klinn-io-ratio header and its gateway's io_ratio come first. New requests follow within about a minute.

tools.name: revoke_key
tools.description:
Revoke a model key

Revokes one of the account's own model keys. It stops working at once. A key that is already revoked, belongs to a customer or does not exist answers 404.

tools.name: get_key_budget
tools.description:
Get a key's budget

One key's budget (any working model key of the account, a customer's included: the keys the `list_budgets` tool lists), each limit with its spend this window. Its monthly limit is the key's monthlyLimitUsd, so a key created with a monthly cap has a budget (hard_stop, no alert). 404 not_found for an unknown or revoked key, or a key without a budget. Windows are UTC: the day from midnight, the week from Monday, the month from the 1st, lifetime from when that limit was set.

id.description: The key id: any working model key of the account, a customer's included (GET /budgets lists them).

tools.name: set_key_budget
tools.description:
Set a key's budget

Sets or replaces one key's budget: daily, weekly, monthly and lifetime limits at our price (at least one), the alert share and the mode. limits.monthly becomes the key's monthlyLimitUsd. hard_stop refuses the key's requests with a 402 once a limit is reached (the request that crosses it can go a little over: the check runs before a request, its cost lands after, and the Model API keeps the key's state for about a minute); alert_only never blocks and sends one email per limit and window when the spend crosses alertPct. The account's budget, when there is one, applies too: the key stops at whichever limit it reaches first. Requests follow within about a minute.

id.description: The key id: any working model key of the account, a customer's included (GET /budgets lists them).

limits.description: Limits in USD at our price, to the cent. At least one; null or left out is no limit.

weekly.description: Per ISO week, from Monday 00:00 UTC.

monthly.description: Per calendar month, from the 1st 00:00 UTC. On a key, this is its monthlyLimitUsd.

lifetime.description: For good, from when this limit was set.

alertPct.description: Email once per limit and window when the spend crosses this share of a limit. 0 turns the alert off.

mode.description: hard_stop refuses requests with a 402 at a limit; alert_only never blocks (it needs alertPct above 0).

idempotencyKey.description: Optional. A unique string so that repeating this call never creates twice.

tools.name: remove_key_budget
tools.description:
Remove a key's budget

Removes one key's budget, its monthly limit (monthlyLimitUsd) included: the key is limited by the account's budget only, if there is one. 204 with no body, also when the key had none.

id.description: The key id: any working model key of the account, a customer's included (GET /budgets lists them).

tools.name: list_ledger
tools.description:
List balance movements

Every movement of the prepaid balance, newest first: top-ups, grants, usage charges (yours and your customers') and adjustments.

cursor.description: The `nextCursor` of the previous page, unchanged.

tools.name: list_management_keys
tools.description:
List agent keys

The account's agent keys (`kl_rs_…`, management keys) for agents and backends, newest first, without their secrets. Active keys only unless `includeRevoked=true`.

tools.name: list_models
tools.description:
List models and prices

Models the Model API serves at a fixed price per token, with our price per million prompt and completion tokens, sorted by id and paged: 100 per page by default, up to 200. `q` narrows the list to models whose id or name contains it (case-insensitive). The list is large: search with q instead of reading every page. Public and cacheable for 60 seconds (`Cache-Control: public, max-age=60`). Call a chat model (kind "chat") at https://api.opencheap.si/v1/chat/completions with a model key, in OpenAI format. Call a decisions model (kind "decisions"), which answers typed questions about a text, at https://api.opencheap.si followed by its `endpoint` with a model key; it is billed on input tokens only.

q.description: Only models whose id or name contains this text, ignoring case (e.g. `claude`, `gpt-4o`).

cursor.description: The `nextCursor` of the previous page, unchanged.

tools.name: get_order_book
tools.description:
Read a model's order book

The model's order book as a seller sees it: the asks by price level, cheapest first (up to 20), what buyers pay and what a seller there earns (buyers pay divided by the fee), how many asks stand at each level, and which level is yours. Price against it: set your own price with the `set_offer_pricing` tool with { price } or follow the market. Refreshed every second; at most 10 reads a second (429 limit_reached). Never a name, a seller or a source. Sellers only: an account that has not accepted the selling terms gets 403 not_seller.

model.description: The model id, e.g. deepseek-v4.1-flash (URL-encode a slash: org%2Fmodel).

tools.name: list_supply_credentials
tools.description:
List saved vendor keys

The account's saved vendor API keys, newest first: the vendor prefix and last four only. Sellers only: an account that has not accepted the selling terms gets 403 not_seller.

tools.name: create_supply_credential
tools.description:
Save your own server or a vendor API key

Saves, for selling, your own OpenAI-compatible server's https base URL and optional key (preset custom), or a vendor API key (today a Z.ai GLM Coding Plan key: preset zai). A preset marked comingSoon in the `list_supply_presets` tool is refused (422 preset_coming_soon). It is sealed at once to the box that serves requests (the console itself cannot read it back), never logged and never shown again: the answer carries a hint only. OAuth and session tokens are refused (400 key_refused). One listing per key: the same key saved again answers 200 with the credential already saved (alreadyAdded: true, nothing new is saved), and a key another account lists is refused (409 key_taken). Then discover its models with the `discover_models` tool. Sellers only: an account that has not accepted the selling terms gets 403 not_seller. At most 20 seller keys per account, and 100 new ones a day: past either, 409 limit_reached.

key.description: The vendor API key (required for a vendor preset; optional bearer key for custom). Sealed at once to the serving box; never stored readable, logged or shown again.

baseUrl.description: custom only: the server's OpenAI-compatible base URL, https and a public host (port 443 or from 1024). Sealed with the key; the serving box checks every address it connects to.

statement.description: The statementVersion of GET /sell/presets: records the seller's statement for this key (else it is asked at publish).

idempotencyKey.description: Optional. A unique string so that repeating this call never creates twice.

tools.name: revoke_supply_credential
tools.description:
Remove a saved key

Removes a saved key: every offer on it is cancelled and it stops serving within a minute (requests already running finish). Sellers only: an account that has not accepted the selling terms gets 403 not_seller.

tools.name: discover_models
tools.description:
Discover a key's models

Reads the models the key can serve and checks that it is a paid or funded key, as a job: poll the `get_supply_job` tool every second until it is done (a few seconds: the model list only); its `models` are every model the key serves, each with its reference price and where it comes from (none anywhere: set your own price), and `paid` false means add funds and discover again. A Z.ai open-platform key (zaiKind open) lists its models as not listable for now: Z.ai open platform keys are coming soon. Each model's self-name check runs in its health test. A discovery running or done in the last ten minutes is reused unless `fresh`. Sellers only: an account that has not accepted the selling terms gets 403 not_seller.

fresh.description: Read the model list again even if it was read in the last ten minutes.

tools.name: rotate_supply_credential
tools.description:
Rotate a saved key

Replaces a saved key with a new key of the same vendor (an own server: a new address or key): sealed like the first, its offers move to it, the old one stops serving within a minute, and a health test runs on the new one. The same key again is a 400. Sellers only: an account that has not accepted the selling terms gets 403 not_seller. A key another account lists is 409 key_taken; one of this account's other keys is 409 key_already_added. At most 100 new seller keys a day per account, rotations included: past it, 409 limit_reached.

key.description: The new key, of the same vendor (custom: the new bearer key, optional).

baseUrl.description: custom only: the server's base URL (the same or a new one).

tools.name: get_supply_earnings
tools.description:
Read selling earnings

Today, 7, 30 and 90 days and the month to date; earnings and requests per UTC day over the range; per offer what it earned, its share of the model's community-served requests, the average discount it gave, the gap to the best offer and whether it is outbid; the newest served requests. Every figure is at least an hour late. Sellers only: an account that has not accepted the selling terms gets 403 not_seller.

tools.name: list_supply_earnings
tools.description:
List served requests

Each request your offers served, newest first: the time to the minute, the model, tokens, your rate and what you earned; at least an hour late, never a buyer or a request id. Sellers only: an account that has not accepted the selling terms gets 403 not_seller.

tools.name: get_supply_job
tools.description:
Read a selling job

A discovery, health test or identity check: its status and, once done, its result. Sellers only: an account that has not accepted the selling terms gets 403 not_seller.

tools.name: list_offers
tools.description:
List offers

Every offer of the account: model, key, status, price, checks, health (the last liveness ping and identity probe), and the model's market as a seller sees it (anonymised levels, the best discount, the gap to it, outbid, whether your ask rests in the book and its rank). Sellers only: an account that has not accepted the selling terms gets 403 not_seller.

tools.name: create_offers
tools.description:
Draft offers from a key's models

Drafts one offer per model of the key's last discovery, priced to follow the market unless a fixed discount is given. The selection replaces the key's drafts. A draft goes live after its health test and identity checks pass (the `test_offer` tool) and it is published (the `publish_offer` tool). Sellers only: an account that has not accepted the selling terms gets 403 not_seller. Send `selfPrices` (model id to { p, c, cr? }, USD per 1M tokens, each above 0) to draft any model at your own price; a model with no reference price anywhere needs one. A Z.ai key that discovery found to be an open-platform one (the job's zaiKind is open) is refused while nothing is listed on it: 422 preset_coming_soon (GLM Coding Plan keys work now). At most 500 offers per account (drafts included, cancelled ones not), and 2,000 new ones a day: past either, 409 limit_reached.

models.description: Models of the key's last discovery (our id or the vendor's). The selection replaces the key's drafts.

selfPrices.description: Your own price for selected models, by model id: { p, c, cr? } in USD per 1M tokens, each above 0. Any model; required for a model with no reference anywhere.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional. A unique string so that repeating this call never creates twice.

tools.name: get_offer
tools.description:
Read an offer

One offer with its status, checks, health and market. Sellers only: an account that has not accepted the selling terms gets 403 not_seller.

tools.name: set_offer_pricing
tools.description:
Price an offer

Follow the market (`match`: one tick under the best offer elsewhere, never past your floor) or set a fixed discount off the reference price, in percent with one decimal (0.1 to 99.9, e.g. 99.5), that follows the reference price when it moves; `maxDiscountPct` is your floor (the lowest price you accept). An offer is served when it is the cheapest healthy source for a request; an ask above our price rests in the book and fills when it is the best available (our routes within our price down, at capacity or over the buyer's limit), never above the model's list price + 5 %. Sellers only: an account that has not accepted the selling terms gets 403 not_seller. Or send `price` for your own price on any model (required for a model with no reference price anywhere): USD per 1M input, output and (optionally) cached input tokens, each above 0, at most one change a second; it is served only when it is the best price for the request, and a market-priced offer switches back with `pricingMode`; buyers see it as the price for the model, and it can change at any time.

pricingMode.description: match follows the market (one tick under the best offer elsewhere, never past your floor); discount and per_model are fixed.

price.description: Your own price (pricingMode self), on any model: USD per 1M tokens, each leg above 0.

cr.description: Cached input (the input price when left out).

tools.name: discard_offer
tools.description:
Discard a draft offer

Deletes a draft that never went live; a listed offer is cancelled instead (the `cancel_offer` tool). Sellers only: an account that has not accepted the selling terms gets 403 not_seller.

tools.name: cancel_offer
tools.description:
Cancel an offer

Ends the offer for good. Sellers only: an account that has not accepted the selling terms gets 403 not_seller.

tools.name: get_offer_health
tools.description:
Read an offer's health log

The offer's health events, newest first: the reason, time to first token (p95), answers and failures in the hour, and an error category. Sellers only: an account that has not accepted the selling terms gets 403 not_seller.

tools.name: pause_offer
tools.description:
Pause an offer

Stops routing to the offer until it is resumed. Sellers only: an account that has not accepted the selling terms gets 403 not_seller.

tools.name: publish_offer
tools.description:
Publish an offer

Lists a draft whose health test and identity checks passed: it goes live within about a minute and is checked continuously from then on. Its key needs the seller's statement on record: pass `statement` (the version from the `list_supply_presets` tool) to accept it. A draft not ready yet, or a key without the statement, is a 409. Sellers only: an account that has not accepted the selling terms gets 403 not_seller.

statement.description: The statementVersion of GET /sell/presets: accepts the seller's statement for the offer's key, if it is not on record yet.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional. A unique string so that repeating this call never creates twice.

tools.name: reset_offer_health
tools.description:
Reset an offer's health

Runs a fresh health test on the key; the offer is routed again once it answers. Sellers only: an account that has not accepted the selling terms gets 403 not_seller.

tools.name: resume_offer
tools.description:
Resume an offer

Routes to a paused offer again. Sellers only: an account that has not accepted the selling terms gets 403 not_seller.

tools.name: test_offer
tools.description:
Test an offer

The health test (one short streamed request on your key, about 16 tokens) and, for a draft, the identity checks (a few hundred tokens). Read the outcome with the `get_offer` tool. A draft that fails either check is deleted (contract v2.4): `get_offer` answers 404 and the job (`get_supply_job`) says why under `removed`; to try again, draft the model again with `create_offers`. Sellers only: an account that has not accepted the selling terms gets 403 not_seller.

retest.description: Test again even when a test ran before (a listed offer's health). A draft that fails is deleted, so it is drafted again instead.

tools.name: bulk_offer_action
tools.description:
Pause, resume, cancel or reset several offers

The same action on up to 100 offers; each one's outcome, so one refusal does not stop the rest. Sellers only: an account that has not accepted the selling terms gets 403 not_seller.

tools.name: get_payout_address
tools.description:
Read the payout address

Where payouts go: the address the seller saved (USDC on Base), when it last changed, and until when a payout to it waits (24 hours after a change), or null. Sellers only: an account that has not accepted the selling terms gets 403 not_seller.

tools.name: get_supply_payouts
tools.description:
Read payouts

Owed, available, requested and paid out, what is held and why, the payout address and the payout history (Requested, Sent with its transaction, Failed or returned). Payouts are sent manually in USDC on Base, usually within 72 hours: `canRequest` says whether one can be requested now and `requestBlocked` why not. Sellers only: an account that has not accepted the selling terms gets 403 not_seller.

tools.name: list_supply_presets
tools.description:
List what a key can be listed for

What a key can be listed for. Today: custom, your own OpenAI-compatible server (any model it serves), and zai with a GLM Coding Plan key. The other vendors (OpenAI, Google AI Studio, DeepSeek, Moonshot, and Z.ai open platform keys) are listed with `comingSoon: true`: a key for one is refused (422 preset_coming_soon). Each vendor carries a one-line terms check (make sure your vendor's terms allow it) and a link to that vendor's terms page. Each carries the short statement the seller accepts before a key goes live (the key is yours, you allow serving other customers' requests, your vendor account is your responsibility) and its version. OAuth and session tokens are never accepted.

tools.name: get_seller
tools.description:
Read the account's seller status

Whether the account sells, its standing and limits. Not a seller yet: `seller: false`.

tools.name: update_seller
tools.description:
Set the seller's daily cap and concurrency

Your own daily earnings cap in USD (resets 00:00 UTC; null for none) and the requests at once per offer (1 to 32). Sellers only: an account that has not accepted the selling terms gets 403 not_seller.

dailyCapUsd.description: USD a UTC day, or null for no cap.

tools.name: create_topup_checkout
tools.description:
Create a card top-up link

A card checkout link (Stripe Checkout) for a person to top up this account. Open the `url` in a browser; the balance is credited when the payment completes. Card top-ups start at $5, in whole dollars, with no maximum of ours: a smaller amount is raised to $5, and the reply returns the limits (maxUsd is Stripe Checkout's own ceiling for one payment, 999999). When a deposit fee applies, it is added on top of the credit (10 % of it plus $0.30 by card): the link charges `payUsd` plus any VAT or sales tax. The amount is fixed: Stripe's page shows the credit as one line, and the fee as its own line when there is one. Takes an agent session or a management key like every v1 operation (a model key gets 403 wrong_key_type), and every call is recorded in the activity log. With an Idempotency-Key, a retry returns the first link instead of making another. Also served at /v1/topup/checkout, which also accepts the account's model keys (kl_live_).

idempotencyKey.description: Optional. A unique string so that repeating this call never creates twice.

tools.name: get_usage
tools.description:
Get usage

Requests, tokens and spend over the last `days` whole UTC days, today included (days=1 is today so far), in total and by day, model and key. Every breakdown counts the same hours, so the totals equal the sum of byDay, of byModel and of byKey. Spend is what the account was charged, at our price, its customers' keys included.

days.description: Window in whole UTC days, today included: 1 to 90.

tools.name: list_wallets
tools.description:
List wallets and invites

Every wallet that signs in to this account with Sign-In with Ethereum (`status: active`), then the wallets invited to join it (`status: invited`). `role` is owner for the wallet that opened an agent's own account and delegate for every other wallet and invite.

tools.name: remove_wallet
tools.description:
Remove a wallet or cancel an invite

Removes an active wallet or cancels an invite. The owner can remove any wallet except its own (409 own_wallet). A delegate wallet can remove only its own wallet: it leaves the account, and its session ends. Anyone else gets 403 owner_only. Removing an active wallet ends its sessions and revokes every key it created (`createdBy: wallet:0x…`): model keys for itself, management keys and keys it made for customers. `revokedKeys` says how many. Returns the remaining wallets and invites.

tools.name: get_whoami
tools.description:
Check who is signed in

The account and the credential behind this request: an agent session (owner or delegate, with its wallet and expiry) or a management key (a delegate), and the permissions it carries. A cheap call to check a credential.
